entries.title: 30 more player skins — Dream SMP, MCC & YouTubers
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now spawn wearing 30 additional real-player skins from the Minecraft streaming and MCC scene — Dream, Technoblade, CaptainSparklez, LDShadowLady, Skeppy and more — bringing the custom-skin pool to 68. Recognizable real-player skins also show up more often: a naturally-spawned PlayerMob now has a 40% chance (up from 30%) of wearing one instead of a vanilla default.
highlights: 30 new skins (pool now 68): Dream SMP, MCC players, and Minecraft YouTubers
Recognizable real-player skins now appear ~40% of the time, up from ~30%
Each skin renders with its correct slim or wide arm model

entries.title: Loved PlayerMobs travel with you on the Dungeon Train
entries.summary: On a Dungeon Train, a PlayerMob that has come to love you now abandons its own fixed route and makes its way to your carriage, settling in once it's with you. Move on down the train and it follows; step off the train and it stays aboard and goes back to its usual wandering.
highlights: A PlayerMob that loves you heads to your carriage instead of marching its own way
Uses the full train toolkit to reach you — stepping through rooms, leaping carriage-group gaps, opening doors, and digging through fill
Relaxes and does its own thing once it shares your carriage; resumes its route if you leave the train
Toggle with the new trainFollowLovedPlayer config option (on by default)

entries.title: Reincarnated echoes wear the player's real skin
entries.summary: "Echo of <name>" PlayerMobs on the Dungeon Train now show the real skin of the player they're an echo of, instead of a default Steve/Alex skin. Their name was already right — now their look matches too.
highlights: Dungeon-Train echoes match the skin of the player they came from
Also fixes the friend-echoes that travel alongside them
The skin is captured at the moment of death, so each echo looks like that player did then
